It is complete and well-formed, but it has no `web` orders at all. `app` and `marketplace` look normal, and every other hour and status is present for them. I did not compare hour or status distributions across all three tables. I found no trailer or row-count metadata, so I can't confirm the expected row count from upstream.

findings.claim: The orders file for 2026-10-01 is structurally clean: 235 data rows, header matches the contract, ends with a newline, no parse problems, and the last line is a full row. It is not cut off mid-row. It is about half the size of 2026-09-30, which had 461 rows and 25,028 bytes against 13,121.

The whole `web` channel is missing on 2026-10-01. `web` normally has about 200–280 orders a day (242 on 09-30) and drops to 0. `app` has 151 (normal range about 120–180) and `marketplace` has 84 (about 52–95). Those two channels sum to 235, matching the file's row count.

Status and hour of day are not the cause. Both remaining channels on 10-01 span roughly 00:23 to 23:55 and have 4 distinct statuses each, the same as on 09-30. The gap is by channel, not by hour range or status. I only checked status counts and hour range in the warehouse, not a full hour-by-hour histogram.
The landing files for orders, order_items and payments show no header or trailer metadata, row-count footer or manifest. The only inspectable fields are the header, row count, bytes and last line.

order_items (464 rows) and payments (219 rows) for 10-01 are well-formed and match the contract. Both end at the same last order as orders, so they look consistent with an orders file that has no `web` orders. Payments (219) is below the orders count (235). I did not compare either file to 09-30 or check which orders have no payment, so that gap is unexplained.

## Verification
- Rerun the partition. `partition_present`, `row_count_trend` and `reconciliation` must pass.
- Row counts for the day are now within the normal range of prior days.
- Hour and channel distributions match prior days.
- `assert_order_totals_match_items` and `assert_payments_match_orders` pass.

## Symptoms
- `ingest` fails: `landing file missing: landing/<table>/dt=<date>/<table>.csv` (loud).
- Check `partition_present:raw.<table>` fails: `raw.<table> partition <date> has 0 rows` (silent: an empty file loads fine).
- Check `row_count_trend:raw.<table>` fails: today's rows fall outside 60%-160% of the trailing 7-partition median.
- Check `reconciliation:raw.orders->marts.fct_orders` fails: distinct raw orders for the day differ from `fct_orders` rows.
- Check `freshness:marts.fct_orders` fails: latest order date in the mart is behind the partition.
- Business symptom: revenue or order count for a day looks too low.

## Symptoms
- dbt tests fail: `unique_stg_orders_order_id`, `unique_stg_order_items_order_item_id`, `unique_stg_payments_payment_id` or similar, with N failing rows.
- `reconciliation:raw.orders->marts.fct_orders` fails: mart row count exceeds distinct raw orders.
- Revenue for a day is inflated; `row_count_trend` may fail on the high side (above 160%).
- Staging models do no dedup, so duplicates in raw flow straight to marts.

## The evidence-citation habit
- Every claim in a ticket or handoff carries an id. Examples:
  - `run 3f2a9c1e, step ingest, log:412`
  - `ops.dq_results check_id=row_count_trend:raw.orders observed=45%`
  - `raw.orders _dt=<date> _source_file=landing/orders/dt=<date>/orders.csv`
- A reader should be able to re-run your queries and see the same thing.
- State what you ruled out, not just what you found.

## Verification
- Rerun the partition. Unique tests pass; reconciliation passes.
- Row count for the day is in the normal range.
- No key in the day's partition also appears in another partition (for cause B).
- Revenue for the day matches the expected level (compare with the trailing median).

args.query: partial export filtered export genuine traffic drop

evidence.text:
## Step 1: Which tables are affected?
- Compare row counts by `_dt` for `orders`, `order_items`, `payments` against the previous 7 days.
- Orders, items and payments are related. A drop in one with others normal suggests a partial export of that table.
- If all three dropped by a similar proportion, the export for the day was truncated or filtered across tables.

## Step 3: Partial vs filtered
- Partial (truncated) export: the file ends early. Rows are cut off by time: early hours present and late hours missing.
- Filtered export: a whole slice is absent regardless of time: e.g. one `channel` or one `status` has no rows, while the rest of the distribution looks normal.
- Compare today's distribution with prior days:
  - orders by hour of `order_ts`
  - orders by `channel`
  - orders by `status`
  - payments by `method`
- A chart or table of share-by-hour and share-by-channel for today vs a typical day makes the gap obvious.
- Record which hours or which category are missing; this is your evidence for the upstream ticket.

## Remedy for one-off export glitches
- Use `request_upstream_redelivery` for the day with ALL affected related tables together: `orders`, `order_items`, and `payments` (add `customers` only if it is also affected).
- Redelivery re-runs the export and produces a correct file for each table.
- Redelivering just `orders` when items/payments were also cut leaves referential mismatches.
- Then rerun the partition and verify.

## Do not
- Do not loosen the 60%-160% threshold to make the check pass.
- Do not insert placeholder rows or copy a previous day's file.
- Do not treat a weekday-pattern day as an incident without checking the same weekday on prior weeks.
- Do not conclude "no data" without checking whether the export ran.

## Step 2: Missing file vs empty file
- Missing: the path does not exist; the error names it. Check whether the export ran at all (other tables present?).
- Empty: header only. `partition_present` fails; trend checks show 0%.

structured.answer: The missing_data runbook covers this. All three tables dropping together points to an upstream export problem, either truncated or filtered, not a single-table glitch. Telling partial from filtered means comparing the hour and channel/status distributions with prior days. A genuine traffic drop is only weakly covered. The runbook gives no explicit test for it beyond the weekday check and confirming the export ran. The fix for an export glitch is upstream redelivery of all related tables together, then a rerun and verification.

findings.claim: The check fails when today's rows fall outside 60%-160% of the trailing 7-partition median, so ~50% is a low-side failure.

If orders, order_items and payments all dropped by a similar proportion, the runbook says the export for the day was truncated or filtered across tables. A drop in only one table suggests a partial export of that table.

Partial (truncated) export: the file ends early, with early hours present and late hours missing. Filtered export: a whole slice is absent regardless of time, such as one channel or status with no rows, while the rest of the distribution looks normal. To tell them apart, compare today's orders by hour, channel and status, and payments by method, with prior days. Record the missing hours or category as evidence for the upstream ticket.

Genuine traffic drop: the runbook has no dedicated section. Its guidance is to check the same weekday on prior weeks before treating a day as an incident, and to confirm the export ran before concluding there is no data. By implication, a real drop would show hour and channel distributions that match normal days, with no missing slice and no cutoff. That is my inference, not explicit runbook text.

Remedy for partial or filtered exports: use request_upstream_redelivery for the day with ALL affected related tables together (orders, order_items, payments; customers only if also affected). Redelivering only orders leaves referential mismatches. Then rerun the partition.

Verification after the rerun: partition_present, row_count_trend and reconciliation pass. Row counts are back in the normal range, and hour and channel distributions match prior days. assert_order_totals_match_items and assert_payments_match_orders also pass.
Do not loosen the 60%-160% threshold, insert placeholder rows, or copy a previous day's file.

findings.claim: Total rows for 2026-10-01 are 235, against 421–534 per day for the prior days (2026-09-25 to 2026-09-30 range 421–534). That is roughly a 50% drop.

By channel, web is 0 on 2026-10-01 versus a 7-day average of 238.4. App is 151 versus 153.6, and marketplace is 84 versus 75.3, both normal. The chart shows web falling from 242 on 09-30 to 0, while the other two lines stay flat.

By hour of order_ts, every hour 0–23 is down by about half (for example hour 0: 6 vs 22.0, hour 12: 12 vs 18.7). No hour is missing, so this is not a time-window truncation. The hour chart shows all four 6-hour buckets falling to about 55–60 from about 100–135.

By status, all four statuses are down by roughly 50–60% (shipped 119 vs 256.6, placed 88 vs 157.9, cancelled 16 vs 25.1, returned 12 vs 27.7). No status disappeared, so the drop is not status-specific.

structured.summary: The 2026-10-01 export from upstream is missing every web-channel order. The orders file has 235 rows against a median of 461, and order_items and payments are also down about 50%. The files are well-formed and not truncated, so this looks like a one-off filtered export. I've proposed redelivering orders, order_items and payments for 2026-10-01, then a rerun.

root_cause.explanation: The orders landing file for 2026-10-01 has 0 rows with channel='web', against about 240 per day normally (242 on 09-30). App (151) and marketplace (84) are normal and sum to 235. Every hour 0-23 and all four statuses are present at about half volume, so the file is not cut off at the end. order_items (464) and payments (219) dropped by the same ~50%. The ingest config is default and no dbt models changed, so the pipeline is not the cause. The row_count_trend checks caught it.

evidence.claim: The quality_checks step failed on row_count_trend for raw.orders, raw.order_items and raw.payments, each at about 50% of the trailing median. Ingest and transform succeeded.
The orders file is complete and well-formed but contains no web orders. App and marketplace are normal, and hours and statuses are all present, so the file was not truncated.
No dbt model changed and the ingest config is default, so a pipeline change is ruled out.
The runbook says to redeliver all affected tables together for a filtered export, then rerun.

alternatives_considered: Partial or truncated export: ruled out because all 24 hours are present and the file is well-formed.

Genuine traffic drop: unlikely, because web falling to exactly 0 while app and marketplace stay normal points to a filtered export. The runbook has no explicit test for this, so my confidence is not higher.
Schema or dbt model change: ruled out because there is no model diff and the ingest config is default.
Loosening the check threshold or rerun_only: the runbook forbids loosening the threshold, and a plain rerun would not bring back the missing data.
Escalating to upstream_app_team: possible if redelivery fails again, but a redelivery request is the safe first step.
